cryptopunks: Ten thousand 24x24 characters given away free in 2017 to anyone with an Ethereum wallet and the patience to claim one. They invented the profile picture.
bored-ape-yacht-club: A swamp club for apes who got rich on crypto and are bored of it. For about eighteen months it was the most valuable membership card on earth.
mutant-ape-yacht-club: Every ape holder got a vial of mutant serum. Drinking it produced a second, uglier ape and doubled the size of the club overnight.
bored-ape-kennel-club: A free dog for every ape. The airdrop that taught the whole market what a companion collection was worth.
bored-ape-chemistry-club: The serum itself, minted as an object. A collection whose entire purpose was to be destroyed to create another one.
azuki: Anime skaters from a studio that understood art direction better than any PFP project before it. Then the founder's abandoned past projects surfaced.
beanz-official: The companion airdrop to Azuki, and briefly worth more than most standalone collections.
azuki-elementals: The sequel mint that took $38M in minutes and shipped art so close to the original that holders revolted within the hour.
azuki-elemental-beans: A companion to the sequel. The tree of Azuki derivatives had by now grown a third branch.
milady-maker: Neochibi girls in a deliberately ugly 2000s internet style, run by an anonymous poster with a difficult history. Elon Musk tweeted one and the floor tripled.
redacted-remilio-babies: The Milady spinoff by the same scene, sold as the boy version. It outlived most of the collections that laughed at it.
doodles-official: Pastel line-art by Burnt Toast, one of the few 2021 collections whose art was legible at thumbnail size. It later spent its treasury on a record label.
space-doodles: Doodles put in rocket ships. The original was locked inside and could be extracted at any time.
moonbirds: Ten thousand owls from a founder with a large newsletter, minted to instant billions and then a long unwinding. Nesting locked them up; a CC0 pivot split the holders.
moonbirds-oddities: The strange ones, airdropped to nesters. Deliberately worse art as a reward for patience.
clonex: RTFKT and Murakami built 3D avatars intended for a metaverse that never opened. Nike bought the studio, then quietly wound it down.
degods: Started on Solana, bridged to Ethereum, deleted its own art twice, and burned its royalties. The most restless blue chip in the market.
mfers: Sartoshi drew a stick figure at a computer, released it CC0, then quit and dissolved his own control of the project. Everyone copied it, which was the point.
nouns: One noun auctioned every single day, forever, with the proceeds going to a treasury the holders vote on. The art lives entirely on Ethereum.
lil-nouns: Nouns, but every fifteen minutes instead of every day, and cheaper. Governance as a firehose.
meebits: Larva Labs followed CryptoPunks with 20,000 voxel characters. The 3D models shipped with them, years before anything could use them.
autoglyphs: The first generative art written entirely into an Ethereum contract. 512 of them, minted in 2019, and the code draws each one on demand.
cool-cats: Blue cats with a friendly line, one of the few 2021 mints that broke out on charm alone rather than a roadmap.
world-of-women: A collection of women, by a woman, at a moment when the market was almost entirely apes and dogs. Reese Witherspoon bought one and the floor moved.
world-of-women-galaxy: The 22,222-piece expansion, airdropped and sold to widen a collection that had become a brand.
veefriends: Gary Vaynerchuk's hand-drawn characters, where the token is a multi-year ticket to his conference. An NFT that is legally a door.
veefriends-series-2: The second series, minted into a market that had stopped believing in the first.
gutter-cat-gang: Street cats with a hard edge, and one of the earliest collections to give holders land and spinoff species.
gutter-dogs: The dogs of the gang, claimed by cat holders. The alley kept expanding.
gutter-pigeons: The third species. By this point the Gutter had a full ecosystem and a real one-block map.
kaiju-kingz: Pixel monsters that breed. Holding two long enough produced a third, which was novel in 2021 and is now standard.
sappy-seals: Sad pixel seals with an unusually stubborn community that kept the project alive through two full bear markets.
pudgy-penguins: Founded by college students, taken from them by the community, and rebuilt into toys sold in Walmart. The only NFT project that became a real consumer brand.
lilpudgys: The little ones, 22,222 of them. The overflow collection that let a sold-out community keep growing.
opepen-edition: Jack Butcher's 16,000 sets of four shapes, revealed slowly through opt-in art drops. A collection that was a years-long performance.
vv-checks: Eighty checkmarks in a grid, sold at $8, satirising Twitter's paid verification. Burning four gives you one with half as many, all the way down to a single check.
terraforms-by-mathcastles: A 20-storey tower of ASCII landscapes rendered entirely by the contract, with music encoded in it. Onchain art at its most ambitious.
fidenza-by-tyler-hobbs: 999 flow-field paintings from Art Blocks, and the piece that convinced the traditional art world that generative code was a medium.
chromie-squiggle-by-snowfro: The first Art Blocks project, by the man who built Art Blocks. A single wave of colour, and the signature of the entire generative movement.
ringers-by-dmitri-cherniak: String wound around pegs, 1,000 ways. Ringers #879 sold at Sotheby's out of the FTX estate for $6.2M.
hashmasks: 16,384 painted portraits by 70 artists, sold on a curve, where holders vote on each mask's name with a token that drips daily.
otherdeed-for-otherside: Yuga's land sale broke Ethereum for a night and burned over $150M in gas. The metaverse it deeded has never fully opened.
the-captainz: Memeland's pirate crew, from the team behind 9GAG. One of the last 2022 mints to hold a serious floor.
the-potatoz: The free Memeland potato that came first and quietly outperformed most of what it was promoting.
chimpers: Pixel chimps with animated idle loops, drawn with more care than the format usually gets.
rektguy: OSF drew a slumped figure in a hoodie after getting wrecked, and 10,000 people recognised themselves in it.
sproto-gremlins: Green gremlins from the Milady extended universe, and one of the few 2023 mints that ran without a roadmap or a promise.
goblintown-wtf: A free mint of hideous goblins with no roadmap, no Discord and a Twitter Space of people screaming. It hit a 7 ETH floor on pure nihilism.
loot: Eight lines of text listing adventurer gear, released free by Dom Hofmann. No art at all — the images were left for other people to build.
more-loot: The uncapped sequel anyone could mint, which proved how much of Loot's value was the scarcity rather than the words.
pixelmon: Raised $70M, then revealed art so bad it became a meme in its own right. It hired real artists and salvaged a fraction of it.
mutant-hounds-by-novel-labs: Stitched-together dogs from the Mutant Cartel, and one of the strongest mints of the 2023 dead zone.
loomlocknft: Wassies: badly drawn blue creatures by an anonymous artist, sold as a joke about crypto traders, and adopted by exactly those traders.
onchainmonkey: 10,000 monkeys generated and stored in a single Ethereum transaction, then later inscribed onto Bitcoin. A collection built to survive its own marketplace.
cyberkongz: Genesis gorillas that paid holders a daily token years before staking was normal, and were among the first to grant clear commercial rights.
nakamigos: A punk-shaped collection released cheap and CC0 in a dead market, which caught a wave nobody expected and briefly did enormous volume.
invisible-friends: Markus Magnusson's walking animated figures. The mint sold out instantly on the strength of a single looping GIF.
deadfellaz: Zombies with a founder who ran the project publicly under her own name, which in 2021 was rare enough to matter.
cryptoskulls: A 2019 collection nobody cared about until 2021, when the market went looking for anything with an old contract date.
mocaverse: Animoca's own membership NFT, sitting at the centre of a portfolio of several hundred gaming companies.
renga: Dan RENGA drew every one of the 10,000 by hand in black and white, refusing traits. Then he kept adding chapters to the story for years.
hv-mtl: Yuga mechs evolved from Bored Ape sewer passes, which were themselves earned by playing a browser game.
cryptoadz: Gremplin's CC0 toads, released with no promises and immediately forked by everyone. The public-domain experiment that actually worked.
cryptodickbutts: A 2021 collection of exactly what the name says, drawn from a decade-old comic, and somehow still trading years later.
0n1force: 7,777 anime spirits with a fully written mythology, from the last quarter of 2021 when a lore document was mandatory.
kanpai-pandas: Pandas with an unusually loyal holder base and a founder who kept shipping long after the market stopped watching.
creepz-genesis: Reptilian invaders running a yield game that paid holders to raid each other. One of the first NFT collections with genuine game theory in it.
chain-runners: Cyberpunk runners rendered entirely by the contract from onchain trait data, with the art generated at read time.
robotos: Friendly robots by Pablo Stanley, whose clean vector style also produced Doodles' closest rival for readability at small sizes.
rug-radio-genesis-nft: Farokh's media network sold membership as an NFT and paid contributors in its own token. Crypto media, funded by its audience.
punks-comic: A comic book about CryptoPunks, sold as an NFT, which is how Pixel Vault turned lore into a franchise before it had one.
mad-lads: Backpack's xNFT collection, minted in a scramble that took Solana's RPCs down. The strongest thing to launch on Solana since the crash.
okay-bears: The bear that carried Solana through the worst month of its history and made the whole chain feel viable again.
solana-monkey-business: SMB: the original Solana blue chip, minted in 2021 when the chain had almost nothing else worth owning.
claynosaurz: Claymation dinosaurs with real 3D animation, from a studio that had actually worked in film.
famous-fox-federation: The foxes that quietly became Solana's utility layer — raffles, missions and tools everyone else used.
degods-solana: The Solana original, before the bridge to Ethereum split the collection in two and started the migration debate.
tensorians: The NFT marketplace that beat Magic Eden at its own game, issued as a collection to the traders who used it.
retardio-cousins: The 2024 Solana meme collection that turned a group chat's in-joke into a genuine cultural moment on the chain.
y00ts-solana: DeGods' sister collection, which took a $3M grant to move to Polygon, then moved again to Ethereum and gave the money back.
abc: A quiet, design-led Solana collection in a market that mostly rewarded noise.
taiyo-robotics: Solana mechs with a long-running story and one of the chain's more elaborate holder ecosystems.
aurory: A Solana game NFT that actually shipped a playable game, which put it in a very small category.
stoned-ape-crew: One of Solana's early narrative collections, and an unusually well-drawn one for its era.
bitcoin-puppets: Deliberately crude puppet drawings inscribed on Bitcoin, run as an anti-project with no roadmap and open contempt for roadmaps.
nodemonkes: One of the first 10,000-piece collections inscribed on Bitcoin, and the one that proved Ordinals could hold a serious floor.
runestone: The largest airdrop in Bitcoin's history, dropped free to over 112,000 wallets and worth hundreds of dollars each within weeks.
ordinal-maxi-biz-omb: OMB: Bitcoin-native PFPs from the earliest days of Ordinals, and a founding piece of that culture.
quantum-cats: Taproot Wizards' cat collection, inscribed to advertise a Bitcoin opcode upgrade. Art as a lobbying campaign.
bitcoin-frogs: Ten thousand frogs inscribed in 2023 that briefly made Bitcoin the highest-volume NFT chain in the world.
ordinal-punks: One hundred punks inscribed in the first 650 inscriptions ever made, traded by hand in a Discord before any marketplace existed.
bitcoin-punks: The full 10,000 punks, re-inscribed onto Bitcoin by someone who simply decided they should be there.
taproot-wizards: Udi Wertheimer inscribed a 4MB hand-drawn wizard, filling an entire Bitcoin block, to make a point about what the chain was for.
rare-sats: Not art at all: individual satoshis with unusual numbers — the first of a block, of a halving epoch, of the whole chain.
btc-degods: DeGods inscribed on Bitcoin, in the season when every Solana project was buying a Bitcoin address.
based-fellas: Base's own pixel crowd, from the stretch in 2024 when the chain's culture was being invented in real time.
onchain-gaias: Fully onchain art on Base with a rare thing for its year: a coherent visual identity and no token.
chonks: Onchain pixel characters on Base whose traits are separate NFTs you can detach and trade, so the character is assembled rather than fixed.
miggles: The Himalayan cat from a Coinbase campaign, which became one of Base's defining memes before its lead left for Robinhood Chain.
wealthy-hypio-babies: The collection that dominated Base through 2024 and then jumped chains to HyperEVM, taking its holders with it.
pixel-pengus: Abstract's pixel penguin derivative, from the chain Pudgy Penguins' own ecosystem helped populate.
final-bosu: Abstract's flagship anime collection, and the first mint on that chain to draw serious outside attention.
bearish: An Abstract collection built around its own streaming culture, where holding was tied to watching.
gigaverse-roms: Access passes to a genuinely popular onchain dungeon crawler — one of the few 2025 game NFTs people actually played.
bullas: Berachain's biggest native collection, minted before the chain's mainnet had proved anything.
beraboyz: Bear PFPs from Berachain's earliest community, when the chain was still mostly a testnet joke.
the-beravote-senate: Governance as a collection: Berachain's voting body, issued as NFTs.
degen: ApeChain's flagship, carrying a name that by 2024 had been used by roughly forty different crypto projects.
not-a-punks-cult: An ApeChain punk derivative whose name is a denial nobody believed.
cyberkongz-genkai-2: CyberKongz moved to Ronin to be near Axie's players, and issued Genkai as its gaming collection.
pixels-pets: Companion pets for Pixels, the farming game that became Ronin's largest by daily active users.
aavegotchi: Ghosts backed by interest-bearing Aave deposits, so every one has a real, redeemable floor. Onchain art with a bank account.
aavegotchi-official-polygon: Ghosts backed by interest-bearing Aave deposits, so every one has a redeemable value underneath the art. DeFi and NFTs, actually fused.
courtyard-io: Real graded trading cards held in a vault and tokenised, which quietly made Polygon a serious NFT chain by volume.
y00ts: The Polygon chapter: a collection that took a grant to move chains, then left again and returned the money.
hypurr-hyperevm: HyperEVM's native cat, from the chain that grew out of the fastest-moving perps exchange in crypto.
illiquid-hyperevm: A collection named after exactly the condition most NFTs were in by 2025.
robinhood-punks: Punks, redrawn for the retail-brokerage chain. The oldest format in the market, arriving on the newest chain in it.
hoodie-pengs: Penguins in hoodies, from the first wave of Robinhood Chain minting in 2026.
opepenhood: Jack Butcher's four shapes, redrawn in Robinhood green by people who had never asked him.
cashcatss: Cats holding money, on a chain built by a company whose entire business is holding money.
much-wow-nft: Hood Dogs: the doge format, arriving on Robinhood Chain about thirteen years late and entirely on purpose.
doginhood-dih: A shiba in a feathered cap. The pun wrote itself and then somebody deployed it.
robinhood-pengs: One of several penguin collections that launched on Robinhood Chain in the same fortnight, none acknowledging the others.
robinhood-kitties: Nine thousand cats on a brokerage chain, in a direct line of descent from CryptoKitties clogging Ethereum in 2017.
hoodini: An escape artist on a chain built for people trying to get out of positions.
hoodle: A doodle derivative on Robinhood Chain, and proof that every format eventually reaches every chain.
broker-punks: Punks in suits. The joke is that the suit is the costume, not the punk.
stonkbrokers-434284142: The r/wallstreetbets aesthetic, finally issued on a chain built by the brokerage that hosted it.
script-kiddies: Fully onchain art on Robinhood Chain, which is a strange place to put a permanence argument.
tall-greys: Aliens, on a brokerage chain, in 2026. Nobody involved has explained this.
degen-dictionary: A glossary of trading slang, minted one term at a time, on the chain where most of it was coined.
